drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. Subject to client approval, we propose a $400,000 annual Base Salary and 12 months of salary severance, together with up to 12 months of employer-paid health-continuation premiums, for termination without Cause or resignation for defined Good Reason. Severance would require an effective release and would remain subject to applicable law. We have deleted the non-compete and proposed the law of the Executive’s principal work state, subject to confirming that state. We would retain customary confidentiality and trade-secret protections without restricting lawful competition. Please let us know whether this package provides a basis to finalize the agreement.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $400,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to required withholding, plus participation in employee benefit plans made available to similarly situated executives, subject to their terms.
edits.name: Compensation counterproposal

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to 12 months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary in regular payroll installments. If the Executive timely elects available continuation health coverage, the Company shall also pay the applicable continuation premiums for the Executive and covered dependents for up to 12 months, ending earlier upon eligibility for substantially comparable coverage from another employer. Severance and premium payments are conditioned on a customary release of claims becoming effective within 60 days following termination; payments shall commence on the first regular payroll date thereafter, with a catch-up payment for intervening installments, subject to applicable tax law. Accrued salary, reimbursable expenses and vested benefits shall be paid independently of the release. “Cause” means fraud, embezzlement, conviction of or a guilty or no-contest plea to a felony involving dishonesty, willful misconduct materially harming the Company, or a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for 30 days after written notice if curable. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in Base Salary, a material diminution of authority or duties, a required relocation of the principal workplace by more than 50 miles, or the Company’s material breach of this Agreement, provided the Executive gives written notice within 60 days after learning of the condition, allows 30 days to cure, and resigns within 30 days after that cure period expires without cure.
edits.name: Severance counterproposal

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY; GOVERNING LAW. No post-employment non-compete restriction shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential information or trade secrets except in performing duties for the Company or as permitted or required by law. This obligation does not restrict use of general skills and experience, information lawfully available to the public, protected whistleblowing, reporting possible violations to government agencies, or other legally protected activity. This Agreement shall be governed by the law of the state in which the Executive principally works, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules and without limiting mandatory protections under applicable law.
edits.name: Replace non-compete and add governing law
